$comment: react-resource-view 0.x → 1.0. One entry per breaking change. Read by `npx react-resource-view migrate`, by the development checks of createViewResource, and written for tools and AIs: apply `from` → `to`; `codemod: false` entries need the `manual` step.

kinds.move: same notion, another place in the declaration
kinds.remove: the key has no replacement — it had no effect, or is built by the library

changes.title: canRead, canList, canCreate, canUpdate, canDelete become one `permissions` object
changes.why: Five keys for one notion, denied by default and silently: a resource declared without them showed a list with no button at all. One object, allowed by default, says only what is restricted.
changes.note: The codemod keeps what a 0.x declaration offered: an action it did not declare was refused, so it is written `false` — only the refusals are written, everything else being allowed. `"readonly"` is used when it fits. Without a `path` there is nothing to export, so `export` is left out. A declaration that named no permission at all is left to the 1.0 default and reported (RV1-PERM-002).
changes.hint: declare `permissions` instead — everything is allowed by default, so only restrictions are written: `permissions: { delete: false }`, `permissions: "readonly"` or `permissions: ["list", "read"]`.

changes.title: Everything is allowed by default
changes.manual: A 0.x resource that declared no `canXxx` at all offered no read, create, update or delete button; in 1.0 it offers them all. The codemod lists these resources (it does not guess): add `permissions` to those that were meant to be read-only.
changes.why: The interface's permissions only decide what is offered; the API is where access is enforced. A deny-by-default protected nothing and broke the first experience — the README example had no button.
changes.before:
createViewResource("books", { path: "/api/books" })
// 0.x: a list with no read, edit or delete button
changes.after:
createViewResource("books", { path: "/api/books" })
// 1.0: every action offered; restrict with `permissions`
changes.note: Where a declaration named at least one `canXxx`, the codemod writes the refusals it implied (RV1-PERM-001).

changes.title: `canList` is read for the list (it was ignored)
changes.manual: Check the lists of resources that declared `canList` differently from `canRead`: the list now follows `canList`, and a refused list protects its page.
changes.why: Bug: `permissionResource` answered the list with `canRead`, so `canList` had no effect.
changes.note: 0.x never refused a list page — `canRead` only hid the read buttons and the way back to the list — so the codemod writes `list: false` only when `canList` said so.

changes.title: `behavior.canExport` becomes `permissions.export`
changes.why: The export is a permission like the others; it sat in `behavior`, away from them.
changes.after: permissions: { export: true } // or nothing: allowed by default
changes.note: The export button still only shows when the resource has a `path` and its dialect describes an export request.
changes.hint: the export is a permission: `permissions: { export: true }` at the root of the resource — and it is allowed by default when the dialect can export.

changes.title: Permission functions receive the record and may be asynchronous
changes.manual: Nothing to change: a function ignoring its argument still works. Use `item` to write rules such as "a finished task cannot be deleted".
changes.why: A rule about one record was impossible to write, and the scope's `authorization` was already asynchronous: one model now.
changes.note: Asynchronous answers are cached per action and record for the time a list is on screen, so a list of 50 rows asks once per row and action.

changes.title: A refused action also protects its route
changes.manual: Check the pages reached by a direct link: `/admin/books/update/1` with `update` refused now shows the scope's `forbiddenFallback` instead of the form.
changes.why: A refused action only hid its button: typing the URL still opened the form.
changes.before: // canUpdate: false — /books/update/1 still drew the form
changes.after: // permissions: { update: false } — /books/update/1 draws the forbidden fallback
changes.note: The fallback is the scope's `forbiddenFallback`, then the configuration's, then a built-in "Access denied".

changes.title: `permissionResource(resource, action, { item, context })` may return a promise; `usePermission` added
changes.to: permissionResource(resource, action, { item, context }): boolean | Promise<boolean>
changes.manual: Calls that used the result as a boolean must handle a promise when a permission is asynchronous — in a component, use `usePermission(action, item)`.
changes.why: A permission can now depend on the record and answer asynchronously.
changes.after: const canUpdate = usePermission("update", item) // false while pending

changes.title: Moving a card on a board asks `permissions.move`, which follows `update` unless declared
changes.from: drop on a board: updateItem, whatever canUpdate said
changes.manual: A 0.x resource that refused `canUpdate` but drew a board still let its cards be dropped in another column; in 1.0 they stay where they are. Add `move: true` to `permissions` to move them without offering the edit form. The codemod marks these declarations with a TODO on `update`.
changes.why: Moving a card writes its record: 1.0 asks a permission for it, as for every other write — but a separate one, so a board can change a status without opening the edit form.
changes.after:
permissions: { update: false, move: true },
views: { list: { layouts: [layout.board({ groupBy: "status" })] } },
changes.note: `move` is a permission like the others — a boolean or a function of the record. Left undeclared, it answers as `update`, so a resource that never mentions it moves its cards exactly when it may update them.

changes.title: `view` disappears: what it held goes to the root of the resource or to `views.list`
changes.why: `view` and `views` differed by one letter, and `view` was typed as a list: `itemsPerPage` and `formFilter` were offered as defaults for every action.
changes.before:
view: {
  name: "Tasks",
  fullWidth: true,
  form: { inputs: TASK_FIELDS },
  formFilter: { inputs: { title: { label: "Search" } } },
  viewVariants: [tableViewOptionFactory({ name: "Table" })],
},
changes.note: `view.name` is dropped when it repeats the resource's `name`, and becomes `views.list.title` otherwise.
changes.hint: `view` is gone. What is common to every action goes to the root of the resource (`form`, `fullWidth`, `components`, `titleField`, `description`, `className`); what belongs to the list goes to `views.list` (`layouts`, `filters`, `pageSize`, `rowActions`).

changes.title: `views[ActionList.update]` becomes `views.update`
changes.why: The keys are plain strings, offered by the autocompletion; there is nothing to import.
changes.note: `ActionList.update` is still accepted wherever an action is expected.

changes.title: `name` of a view becomes `title`, and is derived when not declared
changes.why: The name was declared three times (`name`, `view.name`, `views.list.name`) while the titles were already derived.
changes.note: In development, a `title` identical to the derived one is reported.
changes.hint: a view's title is `title`, and it is derived from the resource's `name` ("Edit — Tasks") — declare it only to say something else.

changes.title: `label` becomes `views.<action>.buttonLabel`
changes.why: An object indexed by action inside a view that is already an action: `views.update.label.create` meant nothing. It only ever labelled buttons.
changes.hint: the text of an action's button is `views.<action>.buttonLabel: "…"`.

changes.title: Root and action are merged deeply
changes.manual: A `views.<action>` that restated a whole object (`components`, `form`, `behavior`) to change one key can now say only that key. One that relied on the shallow merge to *drop* inherited keys must now remove them explicitly: `inputs: { notes: false }`, `components: { top: null }`.
changes.why: `views.update.behavior.closeAfterUpdate` erased the whole `view.behavior`, `openIn` included; the same held for `form`, `components` and `label`.
changes.before:
view: { form: { inputs: FIELDS } },
views: { [ActionList.update]: { form: { inputs: { ...FIELDS, notes: undefined } } } }
changes.after:
form: { inputs: FIELDS },
views: { update: { form: { inputs: { notes: false } } } }
changes.note: Arrays (`layouts`, `rowActions`, `valueOptions`) and functions are replaced, not merged.

changes.title: `itemsPerPage` becomes `views.list.pageSize`
changes.why: A word that belongs to no backend (`itemsPerPage` is API Platform's).
changes.hint: the page size is `views.list.pageSize`.

changes.title: `formFilter` and `defaultFilter` become `views.list.filters` with `initial`
changes.why: The two notions go together and lived apart.
changes.hint: the filters are `views.list.filters: { inputs, initial }` — the filter form and the values applied before any is chosen.

changes.title: `titleKey` becomes `titleField`
changes.why: One suffix for every field option: `titleField`, `dateField`, `colorField`, `statusField`.
changes.note: Typed against the resource's item: a typo is a TypeScript error.
changes.hint: the field naming a record is `titleField` (at the root of the resource, or on a board, gallery, calendar, timeline, tree or map layout).

changes.title: A view no longer declares `id` or `icon`
changes.why: Neither had an effect on a view.
changes.before:
icon: ListTodo,
view: { id: "tasks", icon: ListTodo },
changes.after: icon: ListTodo, // the resource's icon is the one the views use
changes.hint: a view has no `id` or `icon` of its own: the resource's `icon` is used; a layout takes `id` and `icon`.

changes.title: A dialog or a drawer of `read` and `update` links to its full page (`expandable`)
changes.from: no way from a dialog or a drawer to the view's page
changes.manual: Nothing to rewrite. `read` and `update` opened with `open: "dialog"`, `"drawer"` or a frame of one's own — and the records a board opens — now show an "Open in full page" link beside the close button; `create` and `delete` do not. Declare `expandable: false` on a view to take it away, `expandable: true` to add it to `create`.
changes.why: A window too narrow for its record had to be closed, and the record found again by hand.
changes.before:
views: { read: { open: "drawer" } }
// 0.x: no way to the record's page from the drawer
changes.after:
views: { read: { open: "drawer" } } // "Open in full page" in its header
views: { read: { open: "drawer", expandable: false } } // as in 0.x
changes.note: The link is a real link (`<a href>`): Ctrl/Cmd+click opens the page in a new tab. It keeps the layout of the list it was opened from.

changes.title: `behavior` disappears: each option moves to where it has an effect
changes.why: One type shared by the five actions: `closeAfterUpdate` could be written on a list and `bulkActions` on a form, without error and without effect.
changes.after: views: { update: { open: "dialog" } } // closing after a save is what a dialog does
changes.hint: `behavior` is gone: `openIn` → `open`, `closeAfterUpdate`/`refreshDataAfterUpdate`/`redirectToAfterUpdate` → `afterSave`, `rowActions` → `views.list.rowActions`, `canExport` → `permissions.export`, `eventSourced` → `realtime` (root), `openRecordIn` → `views.read.open`, `selectable`/`bulkActions` → `views.list.selectable`/`views.list.bulkActions`.

changes.title: `openIn` becomes `open`: `window` → `page`, `popup` → `dialog`
changes.why: `window` did not mean a new tab and `popup` evoked the browser: the new values describe what is seen. `openIn` was also too close to `openRecordIn`.
changes.hint: `open: "page" | "dialog" | "drawer"` on the action's view (`window` is now `page`, `popup` is `dialog`).

changes.title: `closeAfterUpdate`, `refreshDataAfterUpdate`, `redirectToAfterUpdate` become one `afterSave`
changes.manual: Check forms that combined these options: they could contradict each other, `afterSave` keeps one (redirect, then reload, then close).
changes.why: Three options that could contradict each other; a union makes a contradiction impossible, and the redirection can depend on the saved record.
changes.note: `closeAfterUpdate: false` is the default and is dropped. Defaults: `close` in a dialog or a drawer, `stay` on a page (after a creation, the page moves to the new record, as in 0.x).
changes.hint: what follows a save is `afterSave: "close" | "stay" | "reload" | { redirect: (item) => string }` on `views.create` or `views.update`.

changes.title: `rowActions` moves to `views.list.rowActions`, as strings
changes.why: Only the list has rows.
changes.note: `ActionList.read` is still accepted.
changes.hint: the buttons of a row are `views.list.rowActions: ["read", "update", "delete"]`.

changes.title: `eventSourced` becomes `realtime` at the root of the resource
changes.why: It is a property of the data (Mercure), not of a view.
changes.hint: live updates are `realtime: true` at the root of the resource.

changes.title: `openRecordIn` becomes the `open` of `views.read`; `selectable`, `bulkActions` become options of `views.list`
changes.why: Where a card opens is where the record's `read` view opens: one decision, the same URL from a card, a button or a link. And a selection is the list's, not one layout's: declared once on `views.list`, every layout — table, cards, items, board — selects the same records and offers the same bulk actions.
changes.note: Declared on `view`, on a view or in a layout's `behavior`, `selectable` and `bulkActions` go to `views.list`; a shared fragment of them spread into a layout of the declaration is spread into `views.list` instead, and a layout built away from its resource keeps them, marked `TODO(RV1-BEHAV-006)`. `openRecordIn` goes to `views.read.open`; written on a layout or in a shared fragment, it is reported: declare `views.read.open` on the resource. `selectable` defaults to `true` when `bulkActions` is non-empty, and a board stays selectable for "Move to…".
changes.hint: `openRecordIn` does not exist here: a card opens the record's `read` view where `views.read.open` says. `selectable` and `bulkActions` are options of the list: `views.list.selectable`, `views.list.bulkActions`.

changes.title: `viewVariants` becomes `views.list.layouts`
changes.why: The list is the only action with layouts.
changes.hint: a list's layouts are `views.list.layouts: [layout.table(), layout.board({ … })]`.

changes.title: `tableViewOptionFactory` becomes `layout.table`
changes.why: Seven long imports with inconsistent names (`splitViewFactory` came from `split/columnViewOptionFactory.ts`) for one notion; one `layout` namespace lists them all, each with options named after what they do and typed against the item.
changes.note: `import { layout } from "react-resource-view"`.

changes.title: `cardViewOptionFactory` becomes `layout.cards` (`grid` → `columns`)
changes.why: Seven long imports with inconsistent names (`splitViewFactory` came from `split/columnViewOptionFactory.ts`) for one notion; one `layout` namespace lists them all, each with options named after what they do and typed against the item.
changes.note: `import { layout } from "react-resource-view"`.
changes.hint: this option of `layout.cards` was renamed: `grid` → `columns`.

changes.title: `columnViewOptionFactory` becomes `layout.board` (`identifierKey` → `groupBy`, `identifierKeyList` → `columns`)
changes.why: Seven long imports with inconsistent names (`splitViewFactory` came from `split/columnViewOptionFactory.ts`) for one notion; one `layout` namespace lists them all, each with options named after what they do and typed against the item. `identifierKey` meant "group by".
changes.note: `import { layout } from "react-resource-view"`.
changes.hint: this option of `layout.board` was renamed: `identifierKey` → `groupBy`, `identifierKeyList` → `columns`.

changes.title: `calendarViewOptionFactory` becomes `layout.calendar` (`dateKey` → `dateField`, `endDateKey` → `endDateField`, `titleKey` → `titleField`, `colorKey` → `colorField`)
changes.why: Seven long imports with inconsistent names (`splitViewFactory` came from `split/columnViewOptionFactory.ts`) for one notion; one `layout` namespace lists them all, each with options named after what they do and typed against the item.
changes.note: `import { layout } from "react-resource-view"`.
changes.hint: this option of `layout.calendar` was renamed: `dateKey` → `dateField`, `endDateKey` → `endDateField`, `titleKey` → `titleField`, `colorKey` → `colorField`.

changes.title: `timelineViewOptionFactory` becomes `layout.timeline` (`startDateKey` → `startField`, `endDateKey` → `endField`, `titleKey` → `titleField`, `groupKey` → `groupBy`, `statusKey` → `statusField`)
changes.why: Seven long imports with inconsistent names (`splitViewFactory` came from `split/columnViewOptionFactory.ts`) for one notion; one `layout` namespace lists them all, each with options named after what they do and typed against the item.
changes.note: `import { layout } from "react-resource-view"`.
changes.hint: this option of `layout.timeline` was renamed: `startDateKey` → `startField`, `endDateKey` → `endField`, `titleKey` → `titleField`, `groupKey` → `groupBy`, `statusKey` → `statusField`.

changes.title: `splitViewFactory` becomes `layout.split` (`emptySelected` → `emptyState`, `redirectReadToList` → `readInList`, `resourceAction` → `action`)
changes.why: Seven long imports with inconsistent names (`splitViewFactory` came from `split/columnViewOptionFactory.ts`) for one notion; one `layout` namespace lists them all, each with options named after what they do and typed against the item.
changes.note: `import { layout } from "react-resource-view"`.
changes.hint: this option of `layout.split` was renamed: `emptySelected` → `emptyState`, `redirectReadToList` → `readInList`, `resourceAction` → `action`.

changes.title: `itemViewOptionFactory` becomes `layout.items`
changes.why: Seven long imports with inconsistent names (`splitViewFactory` came from `split/columnViewOptionFactory.ts`) for one notion; one `layout` namespace lists them all, each with options named after what they do and typed against the item.
changes.note: `import { layout } from "react-resource-view"`.

changes.title: A layout's `name` becomes `label`; its URL id is its type
changes.from: layout name (and id = slug of the name)
changes.manual: A layout whose old URL id (`?variant=…`, the slug of its name) differs from its type now answers to its type: `itemViewOptionFactory({ name: "List" })` was `?variant=list`, `layout.items()` is `?variant=items`. A link with the old id falls back on the first layout. Add `id: "list"` to keep it.
changes.why: The id was derived from the name: renaming "Board" to "Kanban" changed the URL and broke the links already shared.
changes.note: The codemod drops a label that only repeats the type ("Table" on a table).
changes.hint: a layout's text is `label`; its URL id is its type (`board`), or `id` to change it.

changes.title: `listComponent`, `rowComponent`, `itemComponent` of a layout become `components.list|row|item`
changes.why: One way to inject a component, everywhere: the `components` object.
changes.after: layout.cards({ components: { row: ProductRow }, frame: false })
changes.note: 0.x drew a card's row component with nothing around it; 1.0 frames it and puts the row's actions under it. The codemod writes `frame: false` on cards that had a `rowComponent`, which leaves the actions out too: remove it from a row that draws no card of its own.
changes.hint: a layout's components are `components: { list, row, item }`.

changes.title: A layout's `form` is merged over the resource's; `fields` picks the columns
changes.to: layout form merged by key; `fields` selects and orders
changes.manual: When a layout's `form.inputs` is not an object literal the codemod cannot list its keys: replace it with `fields: ["title", "status", …]`.
changes.why: Deep merge everywhere, and a column selection reads better as a list of fields than as a second form.
changes.note: The codemod writes `fields` from the keys of the layout's inputs, and keeps the inputs only when they say more than a reference to the same field.

changes.title: Custom layouts: `createView` becomes `layout.custom`, options are read with `useLayout()`
changes.to: layout.custom({ type, components: { list, row, item }, options })
changes.manual: The codemod rewrites a `createView({ … })` call written out in place. A factory of one's own that spreads its arguments into `createView` is left to the hand: rewrite it with `layout.custom`, and read its options in the components with `useLayout().options` instead of `useCurrentViewResourceContext().view`. `npx react-resource-view create-view-variant` writes the new shape.
changes.why: The built-in layouts and yours share one shape; a layout's options are no longer mixed into the view.

changes.title: `layout.board({ openRecord, expandable })` disappears: a card opens `read` where `views.read` says
changes.why: Where a view opens was decided in four places, each with its own default: a board's card, a row's button, the form, the route. It is decided once, by the view: a card, a button and a shared link open the same frame at the same URL, Back closes it and a reload opens it again.
changes.note: A board's card now always opens the record's `read` view — on its page unless `views.read.open` says otherwise. `expandable` is only declared on the view. The codemod moves both to `views.read` when the board is written in the resource's `views.list.layouts`, and reports the boards built elsewhere.
changes.hint: a card opens the record's `read` view where that view says: `views: { read: { open: "drawer", expandable: true } }` instead of `layout.board({ openRecord, expandable })`.

changes.title: `layout.board({ selectable, bulkActions })` disappears: the selection is declared on `views.list`, for every layout
changes.why: A selection is the list's, not one layout's: declared once on `views.list`, every layout — table, cards, items, board — selects the same records and offers the same bulk actions.
changes.note: `selectable` defaults to `true` when `bulkActions` is non-empty; a board stays selectable for "Move to…" unless `selectable: false`. `bulkActions` also takes `"delete"`, the built-in deletion of the selected records. The codemod moves both to `views.list` when the board is written in the resource's `views.list.layouts`, and marks with `TODO(RV1-LAYOUT-014)` those of the boards built elsewhere.
changes.hint: the selection is the list's, for every layout: `views: { list: { selectable, bulkActions } }` instead of `layout.board({ selectable, bulkActions })`.

changes.title: `viewComponent`, `listComponent`, `rowComponent`, `itemComponent` become `components.view|list|row|item`
changes.why: Two injection mechanisms — flat `xxxComponent` keys and a `components` object — for one notion.
changes.hint: components are injected through `components: { view, list, row, item, … }` (at the root, per action or per layout).

changes.title: `decoratorComponent` of a resource becomes `components.wrapper`
changes.why: Same reason: the `components` object is the one way in.
changes.note: The `decoratorComponent` of a scope and of `ResourceViewProvider`'s configuration are unchanged.
changes.hint: the wrapper of a resource's views is `components: { wrapper }`.

changes.title: `components.noResult` becomes `components.empty`
changes.why: Clearer name.
changes.hint: what an empty list draws is `components.empty`.

changes.title: `subViewResource` becomes `tabs`: `list` → `items`, `viewComponent` → `aside`
changes.manual: A `subViewResource` declared on the 0.x `view` reached every action: the codemod puts its tabs on `views.read` and `views.update` — remove the one that had no use.
changes.why: A technical name for what the reader sees as tabs, and `list` designated tabs.
changes.hint: a record's sub-views are `tabs: { orientation, aside, items: [{ resource, filter }] }` on `views.read` or `views.update`.

changes.title: A tab's `slug` → `id`, `name` → `label`, `viewComponent` → `component`, `resourceId` → `resource`, `resourceAction` → `action`
changes.why: The words of the rest of the declaration; `resource` takes the resource or its identifier.
changes.before: { slug: "team", name: "Team", resourceId: USERS_ID, resourceAction: ActionList.list }
changes.note: `resourceAction: ActionList.list` is the default and is dropped.
changes.hint: a tab is `{ id, label, icon, description, resource, action, filter, defaultData, component }`.

changes.title: `onInitViewResource` becomes `filter` and `defaultData` functions of `{ item, parent }`
changes.manual: The codemod rewrites the usual shape — a function ending in `return { ...view, filter: …, defaultData: … }` — and leaves a `TODO(RV1-TABS-003)` on anything else.
changes.why: To filter a tab on its parent one had to rebuild and return the whole view context.
changes.after:
filter: ({ item }) => ({ author: (item as User | undefined)?.name }),
defaultData: ({ item }) => ({ author: (item as User | undefined)?.name }),
changes.note: `item` is typed after the resource the tabs are declared on: `({ item }) => ({ author: item.name })` is enough once the cast is no longer needed.
changes.hint: a tab is narrowed to the record with `filter: ({ item }) => ({ … })`, and `defaultData: ({ item }) => ({ … })` presets what is created from it.

changes.title: Without `path`, `storage: "local"` must be declared
changes.why: Forgetting `path` switched to `localStorage` without a word: one believed to talk to the API while the data stayed in the browser.
changes.note: The codemod adds `storage: "local"` to a declaration with no `path`, unless it replaces all five repository methods or draws a screen of its own (`components.view`). Without `path`, `storage` or a complete `repository`, development throws an error naming the resource.

changes.title: `preGetCollection`, `preGetItem`, `preCreate`, `preUpdate` become `hooks.beforeList|beforeRead|beforeCreate|beforeUpdate`
changes.why: Only "before" hooks existed, flat among the options; `preCreate` and `preUpdate` lost the view context on the way to the repository (bug fixed).
changes.note: Hooks may now be asynchronous, and always receive `{ viewResourceContext }`. New: `beforeDelete`, `afterSave`, `afterDelete`.
changes.hint: code around the data goes in `hooks: { beforeList, beforeRead, beforeCreate, beforeUpdate, beforeDelete, afterSave, afterDelete }`.

changes.title: Repository methods move to `repository`
changes.why: The repository methods were offered by the autocompletion of the declaration, mixed with its options.
changes.before: getItem: async ({ id }) => ({ data: await fetchBook(id) }),
changes.note: The built resource still exposes `resource.getItem(…)` and the others, decorated with the hooks.
changes.hint: a hand-written data access goes in `repository: { getCollection, getItem, createItem, updateItem, removeItem }`.

changes.title: `limit` becomes `quota` (`getLimit` → `get`)
changes.manual: A `fallback` component receives `{ quota }` instead of `{ limit }`; the runtime context parameter `limit` is `quota`; `useLimit` is `useQuota`.
changes.why: `limit` read like pagination; it is the number of records that may be created.
changes.before: limit: { getLimit: (ctx) => ({ current: count(ctx), max: 3 }), fallback: Upgrade },
changes.after: quota: { get: (ctx) => ({ current: count(ctx), max: 3 }), fallback: Upgrade },
changes.hint: the creation quota is `quota: { get: (context) => ({ current, max }), fallback }`.

changes.title: `resourceBuild`, `onChange` and `@type` are no longer declared
changes.why: What the library builds was offered in the autocompletion of what one writes.
changes.note: `resource.onChange` still exists on the built resource.
changes.hint: this key is built by `createViewResource` and cannot be declared.

changes.title: Writes are drawn before the API answers (`optimistic`)
changes.from: every write waits for the API before the list changes
changes.manual: Nothing to rewrite, but the perceived behaviour changes: a saved form, a deleted row, a cell edited in place, a card moved and the writes of `bulkActions` made through their `mutation` argument show in the list before the API answers — a created row appears, marked as being saved, before it has an id. A refusal puts the row back with a toast; a form keeps the API's violations on its fields. Declare `optimistic: false` at the root of a resource, or on one action (`views.delete: { optimistic: false }`) where the list must wait for the server — an in-place edit and a card moved are updates.
changes.why: Every write waited for the API before anything moved, and only the board's drag and drop did otherwise.
changes.before:
createViewResource("tasks", { path: "/api/tasks" })
// 0.x: a deleted row stays until the API has answered
changes.note: The API's answer replaces the guess as soon as it comes (generated id, computed fields); several writes to one record show the last one; a list read again while a write is in flight — a realtime push — keeps the row as written. `useResourceMutation(resource)` gives an application's own actions the same optimism and rollback; `BulkActionInterface.onAction` receives it as its second argument.

changes.title: A resource no longer declares its `scope`: the scope lists it in `resources`
changes.manual: Make sure every resource the codemod reports is listed in the `resources` of its scope (`npx react-resource-view migrate` prints them). A resource listed nowhere links within the current scope.
changes.why: The scope was declared three times: `resource.scope`, `scope.resources` (which nothing read) and `createItemMenuWithResource({ scope })`.
changes.note: The scope stamps its resources when it loads; `resource.scope` is still readable on the built resource.
changes.hint: a resource does not name its scope: list it in the `resources` of the scope instead.

changes.title: A scope's `menu` takes resources directly, or `"auto"`
changes.why: `createItemMenuWithResource` ran when the scope module was read, before any scope was known: without `resource.scope`, its links would point at the wrong area.
changes.note: The codemod rewrites the calls found in a `menu` (or a group's `items`). `createItemMenuWithResource` is still exported, for menus built outside a scope — pass it the `scope` then.

changes.title: `setResourceConfig({ defaultResource })` becomes `configureResourceView({ defaults })`
changes.manual: `getResourceConfig` is gone; read the defaults with `getResourceViewDefaults()`.
changes.why: The merge was shallow — passing a `defaultResource` erased the default components (the table…) — and `defaultResource.views` was read for `openIn` only, the rest silently ignored. `defaults` has the shape of a declaration and is merged deeply into every resource.

changes.title: What one writes is `ResourceDefinition`, what the library builds is `ViewResource`
changes.manual: Code reading a built resource's old keys (`resource.canUpdate`, `resource.view`) must read `resource.permissions` and `resource.views`.
changes.why: `ResourceOptionInterface = Partial<ViewResourceInterface>` offered `resourceBuild`, `onChange`, `@type` and the repository methods in the autocompletion. The new public types drop the `Interface` suffix.

changes.title: `ViewInterface`, `ViewListInterface`, `ViewUpdateInterface` are replaced
changes.manual: A declaration fragment is typed with the definition of its action (`UpdateViewDefinition<Task>`); a component reading the context's view gets a `ResolvedView`.
changes.why: One type per action, so each only offers what has an effect there.

changes.title: The context's `view` is the resolved view
changes.manual: Custom components reading the context's view: `view.name` → `view.title`, `view.rowComponent` → `view.components.row`, `view.viewVariants` → `view.layouts`, a layout's options (`view.identifierKey`, `view.grid`…) → `useLayout().options`, `view.behavior.openIn` → `view.open`.
changes.why: The context exposes what the declaration means, with the same words.
